blame_edge.commit_id.owner: the worker that mints the commit DAG (commit_obj / commit_edge / ref)
blame_edge.commit_id.reason: An edge is bound to the commit that landed the edit, and no commit exists yet.

blame_edge.evidence_quote_sha256.reason: CHECK asserted_needs_quote requires the digest of an exact, unique substring of a document that has not been rendered. The quote_ref names which sentence to bind; the corpus does not invent the sentence.

blame_edge.p_link.owner: recall lane calibration (isotonic fit on the adjudicated set)
blame_edge.p_link.reason: CHECK scored_needs_features requires p_link on every non-asserted basis. It is the output of a calibration this corpus does not perform; the features it would be computed from are emitted in full on the edge. Supplying a plausible probability would launder a calibration one hop upstream, which is the same defect class as writing a projected column.

blame_edge.review_sig.reason: CHECK human_needs_signature guards the only column proving a human was in the loop. A fixture signature would make it unfalsifiable, which is worse than an absent one.

clause.birth_commit.owner: the worker that mints the commit DAG (commit_obj / commit_edge / ref)
clause.birth_commit.reason: commit_id is sha256 over the JCS envelope and cannot be chosen. Nothing in the corpus lane mints commits, so every clause points at a commit that does not exist yet and says so rather than inventing thirty-two bytes.

clause_version.canon_text.reason: History first, text second. raw_text, canon_sha256 and anchor_set follow from the same act of rendering this clause and are closed with it. Every offset in this system is into canon_text, so a digest of anything else would make every span in the corpus point at the wrong sentence.
